title: November 11: native setpoint excitation (V26) and the proposed V27 cable/ring branch
summary: GeometricNeuronOriginReview is an archival causal review, not a numbered implementation. SurfaceListener (V26) reuses the audited feedback oscillator to study state-dependent surface listening, endogenous setpoint-port excitation, constant-dependent operating regimes, and a reliable but hand-wired one-way relay; the same setup does not yet learn, provide true refractory protection, or demonstrate persistent information. At this early checkpoint GeometricNeuronV27 contained only a licence and its ring/cable work was an untested proposal. Its later native ring, erase, and V28 experiments are documented in the November 11 follow-up pass.

nodes.claim: V26: a ten-round continuation of the audited Perception Lab geometric feedback loop, using moving checkerboard coupling and the original Homeostatic Coupler setpoint_mod input to study inter-unit excitation, oscillator/relay operating regimes and one-way transmission.
nodes.survived: With setpoint_mod open, the reduced native.py returns the original loop when uncoupled (parity test), and an arriving two-tap signal can elicit a receiver-generated beat without output override. At constant 1.6, otherwise silent followers relayed a one-way chain at weight -6 with 300/300 reaches and 4 ticks per hop; an eight-unit chain relayed 50/50 observed beats. The constant sweep finds self-beating and silent-but-excitable regimes. These are source-reported code/test results, not independent Genealogy reruns.
nodes.killed: The checkerboard's apparent special spatial code has not been isolated from scalar square-size dynamics. Moving-surface coupling could silence a colony, and merely removing the isolated-unit saw worsened it. The one-way chain uses hand-set constants and weights, bidirectional wiring runs away, and the silent relay responds without an absolute refractory period. No endogenous learning, long-term memory, physical dendritic cable or biological neuron has been established.

nodes.claim: At the first November 11 checkpoint V27 was only a proposal; later on November 11 it implemented fixed cable delay/attenuation and native ring-memory tests using the unchanged original 2025 Perception Lab/V26 feedback loop. The evidence is recorded in the separate follow-up.
nodes.survived: Later V27 results report 40/40 sampled random patterns preserved for 1000 laps for eight- and sixteen-relay rings; longer delay-cable loops also regenerated stored events; one-tick setpoint_mod +12 erased exactly the selected event in 12/12 tests. These are source-reported, not independently rerun.
nodes.killed: Dense all-ones patterns can change the 50-tick variance regime and corrupt memory; some shorter rings fail long retention. Fixed cable lengths and couplings are engineered, and classical delay-line storage predates this work. Native GN27 has no demonstrated new learning rule or capacity advantage.

edges.why: SurfaceListener's gn/core.py retains the reduced 59-tick ECG colony from the ReturnToGeometricNeuron work, while native.py reopens the original setpoint_mod port and the later coupling/receptor experiments are declared additions.

The archived origin-review graph and causal reconstruction are the reference for SurfaceListener's ten-round studies; the review itself is an audit and preservation repository, not a new physical neuron generation.

motifs.title: Native excitability and event relaying do not by themselves create stored information
motifs.description: A fixed homeostatic coupler changes from spontaneous clock to excitable relay as its setpoint constant changes. The sender's beat can drive the receiver through a port already present in the original graph, yet one-way transmission with manual weights, runaway bidirectional excitation and loss of activity when the input stops do not establish learning or persistent memory. V27 was proposed at this checkpoint but later implemented measured ring memory, recorded in a separate November 11 follow-up.
